newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African institutions lighten local investments.
newsitem.headline: S.African institutions lighten local investments.

text.p: South African institutions lightened their weightings in most domestic investment categories to divert funds offshore in the first quarter of this year, results of First Bowring's asset allocaton survey shows.

The survey by the actuarial firm, released on Wednesday, showed that insurers' investment in equities, property, fixed interest stocks and cash all dipped in the first quarter from the fourth quarter of last year.
At the same time, insurers invested 3.0 of their total 42.39 billion rand of funds offshore.
Investors also lightened their weightings in all categories, barring fixed interest, and had 1.8 percent of the total 97.94 billion rand of funds under management invested offshore.
Among insurers, Old Mutual was the most aggressive investor in offshore markets, investing between 8.5 and 9.2 percent of total assets abroad in the first quarter.

In his budget last month, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced that the 10 percent limit on local acquisition of foreign portfolio assets would apply to all assets under management in any specific unit trust fund.
Among investors, Coronation topped the offshore investment category with 4.7 percent of funds under management invested abroad.
The total amount of funds invested by both insurers and investors increased by 5.6 percent to 140.33 billion rand.

Combined asset allocation in equities dipped to 64 percent from 65 percent in the previous quarter, property eased to 4.3 percent from 4.7 percent, fixed interest edged up to 21.6 from 21.5 and cash slipped to 8.1 percent from 8.8 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996.
No weighted average was provided for the foreign assets as this is the first time First Bowring has included these statistics in its survey.
